princessDiana.title: Princess Diana
princessDiana.intro: Diana, Princess of Wales, became one of the most famous people in the world. She used her fame to support charities, fight the stigma around HIV/AIDS and campaign against landmines.
princessDiana.coverAlt: Placeholder illustration of a royal crest with roses

timeline.title: Order Her Story
timeline.description: Put the key moments of Diana's life in the right order.
instructions: You will see six events from Diana's life in random order.
Drag and drop the cards, or use the arrow buttons on mobile.
Press Check to see your score and learn about each event.

events.label: Diana Frances Spencer is born at Park House, Sandringham, England.
events.explanation: Diana was born on 1 July 1961 into an aristocratic family. Her father later became the 8th Earl Spencer.

events.label: She marries Prince Charles at St Paul's Cathedral in London.
events.explanation: The wedding took place on 29 July 1981 and was watched on TV by an estimated 750 million people around the world.

events.label: Her first son, Prince William, is born.
events.explanation: Prince William was born on 21 June 1982. Her second son, Prince Harry, was born in 1984.

events.label: She shakes hands with an HIV/AIDS patient without wearing gloves.
events.explanation: In April 1987, at London Middlesex Hospital, this simple gesture helped show the world that HIV is not spread by touch.

events.label: Diana and Charles officially divorce.
events.explanation: The divorce was finalised on 28 August 1996. Diana kept the title Diana, Princess of Wales.

events.label: She walks through a minefield in Angola to raise awareness about landmines.
events.explanation: In January 1997 she visited Huambo, Angola, with the HALO Trust. Her campaign helped build support for the international treaty banning landmines.

differences.title: Find the Differences
differences.description: Spot the five changes between two royal tea room pictures.
instructions: Compare Picture A and Picture B carefully.
Click or tap on a difference in either picture.
Find all five differences to win. Wrong clicks count as misses.
differences.imageAlt: Placeholder illustration of a royal tea room with a window, a clock, a bookshelf and a table

quiz.title: How Much Do You Know About Diana?
quiz.description: Ten questions about the life and work of the People's Princess.
instructions: Answer ten multiple-choice questions.
Each question has four options and only one is correct.
You get instant feedback and a short explanation.

questions.q: In which year was Diana born?
questions.explanation: Diana was born on 1 July 1961 in Sandringham, Norfolk.

questions.q: What was Diana's family name before she married?
questions.explanation: She was born Diana Frances Spencer, daughter of John Spencer, who became the 8th Earl Spencer.

questions.q: Where did Diana and Prince Charles get married in 1981?
questions.explanation: They married at St Paul's Cathedral in London on 29 July 1981.

questions.q: What job did Diana have before her engagement?
questions.explanation: She worked as an assistant at the Young England Kindergarten in Pimlico, London.

questions.q: Who designed Diana's famous wedding dress?
questions.explanation: British designers David and Elizabeth Emanuel created the dress, which had a 25-foot (about 7.6 m) train.

questions.q: What was the name of Diana's first son?
questions.explanation: Prince William was born in 1982. Prince Harry followed in 1984.

questions.q: In 1987, Diana helped fight the stigma around which illness by shaking a patient's hand without gloves?
questions.explanation: At the time, many people wrongly believed HIV could be spread by touch. Her gesture changed public attitudes.

questions.q: In which year did Diana and Charles divorce?
questions.explanation: They separated in 1992, and the divorce was finalised in August 1996.

questions.q: Which cause did Diana support by walking through a minefield in Angola in 1997?
questions.explanation: Her visit with the HALO Trust drew global attention. The Ottawa Treaty banning anti-personnel landmines was signed in December 1997.

questions.q: Which popular nickname is Diana remembered by?
options: The Queen of Hearts of Europe
questions.explanation: British Prime Minister Tony Blair called her "the People's Princess" in a speech in 1997.

oceanGate.title: OceanGate & the Titan
oceanGate.intro: In June 2023, the submersible Titan, operated by the company OceanGate, imploded during a dive to the wreck of the Titanic. All five people on board lost their lives. This section looks at the facts and the engineering lessons, with respect for the victims.
oceanGate.coverAlt: Placeholder illustration of the deep ocean with light rays

submarine.title: Submarine Adventure
submarine.description: Guide a small sub down to 20 m without hitting obstacles.
instructions: Steer the submarine down to the target depth of 20 m.
Use the arrow keys or W A S D. On mobile, use the on-screen buttons.
Avoid rocks and jellyfish. A collision ends the dive.

timeline.title: Timeline Challenge
timeline.description: Order the documented events of OceanGate and the Titan.
instructions: You will see six documented events in random order.
Drag and drop the cards, or use the arrow buttons on mobile.
Press Check to see your score and read a short explanation of each event.

events.label: OceanGate is founded in the United States by Stockton Rush and Guillermo Söhnlein.
events.explanation: The private company, based in Everett, Washington, planned to take paying customers on deep-sea expeditions.

events.label: Industry experts and a company employee raise safety concerns about Titan's design and testing.
events.explanation: A former director of marine operations wrote a critical report, and more than 30 experts from the Marine Technology Society signed a letter warning about the experimental approach.

events.label: Titan makes its first crewed expeditions to the wreck of the Titanic.
events.explanation: The Titanic lies about 3,800 m (12,500 ft) deep in the North Atlantic, about 600 km south of Newfoundland, Canada.

events.label: Titan starts a dive to the Titanic with five people on board and loses contact with its support ship.
events.explanation: Communication was lost about 1 hour and 45 minutes into the descent, starting a large international search.

events.label: The US Coast Guard announces that debris from Titan was found near the Titanic.
events.explanation: The debris was consistent with a catastrophic implosion of the pressure hull. All five people on board died.

events.label: The US Coast Guard investigation board holds public hearings and later publishes its final report.
events.explanation: The Marine Board of Investigation held hearings in September 2024. Its 2025 report concluded the tragedy was preventable and pointed to problems in design, testing and safety culture.

detective.title: Engineering Investigation
detective.description: Act as a safety inspector: which cases are real red flags?
instructions: Read six short cases about engineering, safety and risk management.
Some are documented facts about Titan, others are clearly labeled fictional scenarios.
Select every case you think is a real red flag, then press Check.

cases.text: The submersible was never certified ("classed") by an independent organization such as DNV or ABS.
cases.explanation: Independent classification means outside experts review the design, materials and tests. Skipping it removes an important safety check.

cases.text: The main pressure hull was made of carbon fiber composite, a material with little track record for repeated deep dives.
cases.explanation: Carbon fiber is very strong, but under repeated extreme compression, hidden damage can build up. Using it without extensive testing was a serious risk.

cases.text: In 2018, the company's director of marine operations wrote a report with safety concerns about hull testing and was later dismissed.
cases.explanation: When an expert inside the company warns about safety, the concerns should be investigated, not ignored. A healthy safety culture listens to warnings.

cases.text: An acoustic monitoring system was installed to listen for cracking sounds in the hull during dives.
cases.explanation: Monitoring by itself is a reasonable extra safety measure. The problem appears only if it is used instead of proper testing, because it may give very little warning time.

cases.text: A dive team completes a full pre-dive checklist and cancels the dive because the weather is worse than the safety limit.
cases.explanation: This is good practice. Clear limits and the willingness to cancel are signs of a strong safety culture.

cases.text: A company tests a full-scale model of its hull to destruction in a pressure chamber to confirm a large safety margin before carrying passengers.
cases.explanation: Testing beyond the operating depth with a safety margin is exactly what engineers should do before putting people inside.

halloween.title: October 31 — Halloween
halloween.intro: Celebrate October 31 with three spooky challenges! Test your candy-catching reflexes, uncover haunted memory pairs, and survive a misty night avoiding eerie creatures.
halloween.coverAlt: Halloween illustration of a carved glowing pumpkin and bats under a full moon

catchCandies.title: Catch the Candies
catchCandies.description: Control a spooky pumpkin basket and catch falling sweets before they hit the ground.
instructions: Catch 20 candies to win. Avoid bad items (💀, 💣, 🕷️) — they cost 1 life!
Your basket shrinks as you catch sweets. Speed scales up smoothly.
Use Left/Right arrow keys, A/D, touch the on-screen buttons, or drag your basket.
Reaching 20 candies wins the game! You can then play an optional Hard Bonus Mode.

memory.title: Terrifying Memory
memory.description: Match all 8 pairs of haunted Halloween symbols before dawn breaks.
instructions: Click or tap any card to reveal its spooky Halloween character.
4x4 grid = 8 pairs. You have 120 seconds and a maximum of 60 flips!
Complete all 8 pairs to win!

surviveNight.title: Survive the Night
surviveNight.description: Navigate a misty graveyard path and travel 25 meters while dodging spooky hazards.
instructions: Travel forward through the haunted mist to reach the 25-meter safety haven.
You start with 3 lives. Collisions grant 1000ms invulnerability.
At 20m, a final chaser pursues you! The walls narrow every 15m.
Steer with arrow keys, WASD, or on-screen directional buttons.
